directions.headline: I have closed formulas for every two-loop theta kernel on R^T x C^H, T = 0 or 1, for all D <= 6, with general sources at N and at the interior vertices, and with the root either at a trivalent vertex or at an interior one. At T = 1 the Schwinger-space density is (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} D_theta/(2U^{H+3/2}): it depends on t only through U and does not depend on lambda_N. At T = 0 the density is (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} R_A R_B R_C Q(L(t))/U^{H+2}. At z = 0, K^{T=1} = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} (D_theta/2) prod_P Gamma(H+3/2-n_P)/(Gamma(H+3/2) prod_P (n_P-1)!), so the expected formula is right up to this sign. K^{T=0} = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} prod_P (H-n_P)!/((H+1)! prod_P (n_P-1)!) Q(Lbar), where Lbar = sum_v mu_v lambda_v and mu_v = (edges from v to N')/n_P. Both are in the cycle basis C3 = (A-B, B-C); the htk basis adds (-1)^{(q+1)D}. Every closed form matches my own exact brute-force Kirchhoff computation pointwise, sign included, on all 32 graphs. The z = 0 values also match htk.kernel_exact, 55 moments of order <= 2 in y (the z-Taylor coefficients) match it, and the values reproduce S1 1/24, S2 (A) and (B), S3 c_pqr and the S4 ladder value -1/432. claims.statement: Notation (labelling of htk.graph.theta, same as S3 Section 7). The trivalent vertices are N = 0 and N' = root. Paths P in {A,B,C} have n_P = p,q,r edges P_1..P_{n_P}, oriented N -> N'; edge order A,B,C; interior vertex P_k sits between edges P_k and P_{k+1}, with source lambda^P_k; Lambda_P is the H x (n_P-1) matrix of these sources. Cycle matrix C3 has rows A-B and B-C. Definitions: R_P = sum_j t_{P_j}, x^P_j = t_{P_j}/R_P, sigma^P_k = sum_{j>k} x^P_j, w_P = (1/R_P)/sum(1/R), U = R_A R_B + R_B R_C + R_C R_A, Q^P_j = sum_{k<j} lambda^P_k, mhat_P = sum_k sigma^P_k lambda^P_k, L = lambda_N + sum_P mhat_P. Currents: y_{P_j} = w_P L - mhat_P + Q^P_j (S3 eq-series, eq-parallel). Determinants (2H x 2H, (a;b) is a column with top block a and bottom block b): D_theta = det[(Lambda_A;0),(Lambda_B;Lambda_B),(0;Lambda_C)] and Q(v) = det[(v;0),(0;v),(Lambda_A;0),(Lambda_B;Lambda_B),(0;Lambda_C)]. K[C3] is the reduced kernel with cycle matrix C3; K_htk is the reduced kernel with htk's positively oriented basis.

Derivation chain. (1) phi^i_P = sum_j y^i_{P_j} dt_{P_j} = V^i dlog R_P + R_P dmhat^i_P, with V = L/sum_P(1/R_P). Then psi_1 = phi_A - phi_B = V a + R_A dmhat_A - R_B dmhat_B and psi_2 = V b + R_B dmhat_B - R_C dmhat_C, where a = dlog(R_A/R_B), b = dlog(R_B/R_C), a^b = Omega_R/(R_A R_B R_C) and Omega_R = R_A dR_B dR_C - R_B dR_A dR_C + R_C dR_A dR_B. (2) prod_i psi^i_1 psi^i_2 = (-1)^{H(H-1)/2} R_*^2 prod_P R_P^{n_P-1} E(L) a^b^dsigma + (terms without a^b), with R_* = 1/sum_P(1/R_P) and E = det[(L;0),(0;L),(Lambda_A;0),(-Lambda_B;Lambda_B),(0;-Lambda_C)] = (-1)^{H+q} Q(L). The pure fibre part is (-1)^{H(H-1)/2+H+q-1} prod_P R_P^{n_P-1} D_theta dsigma. (3) iota_E vol = (-1)^{q-1} prod_P R_P^{n_P-1} Omega_R ^ dx, using prod_j dt_{P_j} = R_P^{n_P-1} dR_P dx^P_2..dx^P_n and dsigma = dx. (4) rho_2 = Omega_R/(2U^{3/2}) (S3 eq-rho2 with M11 = R_A+R_B, M12 = -R_B, M22 = R_B+R_C); it is top degree in R, so only the fibre part of prod psi enters. (5) Chart R_P = 1/w_P: U = 1/(w_A w_B w_C), |det[t; dt/dxi]| = prod_P w_P^{-(n_P+1)} with sign (-1)^{q-1}, xi = (w_A, w_B, x^A_2.., x^B_2.., x^C_2..).

Schwinger-space densities for cycle matrix C3 and edge order A,B,C. T=1: D(t) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} D_theta/(2 U^{H+3/2}); this depends on t only through U and does not depend on lambda_N. T=0: D(t) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} R_A R_B R_C Q(L(t))/U^{H+2}, with L(t) = lambda_N + sum_{P,k} sigma^P_k(t) lambda^P_k. For any other labelling, orientation or edge order: D_G = sgn(pi_std) D_std, where pi_std lists the graph's edges in A,B,C order (C_re y_e is invariant under edge reversal).

Items (a), (b), (c), integral representations over Delta^2 x prod_P Delta^{n_P-1}, with d^2w = dw_A dw_B and dx = prod_P dx^P_2..dx^P_{n_P} (Lebesgue). K^{T=1}[C3](lambda;z) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} (D_theta/2) Int d^2w prod_P w_P^{H+1/2-n_P} Int dx exp(sum_v lambda_v.X_v). K^{T=0}[C3](lambda;z) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} Int d^2w prod_P w_P^{H-n_P} Int dx Q(L(x)) exp(sum_v lambda_v.X_v). The exponents satisfy H+1/2-n_P >= -1/2 and H-n_P >= 0, since n_P <= D. For H=5, T=1 this is S3 eq-Ktheta, with K^S3 = -K_htk = -K[C3].

Item (c), displacement points. Let Z_P = sum_j z_{P_j} along N -> N' and W = sum_P w_P Z_P. Then -sum_e y_e.z_e = sum_v lambda_v.X_v with X_N = -W, X_{P_k} = sigma^P_k (Z_P - W) - sum_{j>k} z_{P_j}, X_{N'} = 0. For a root at an interior vertex rho: X^(rho)_v = X_v - X_rho.

Item (a), T=1 at z=0. K[C3](lambda;0) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} (D_theta/2) prod_P Gamma(H+3/2-n_P) / (Gamma(H+3/2) prod_P (n_P-1)!) and K_htk = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+(H+1)(q+1)} times the same; (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} = (-1)^{ceil(H/2)}. The expected formula is therefore correct in magnitude, holds for an arbitrary source at the non-root trivalent vertex N (no dependence on lambda_N), and carries the sign shown. Values of c1 = K/(pi D_theta): H=0 (1,1,1): 1; H=1 (1,2,2): 1/3; H=2 (1,3,3), (2,2,3): 1/20, 1/30; H=3 (1,4,4), (2,3,4), (3,3,3): 1/252, 1/420, 1/840; H=4 (1,5,5), (2,4,5), (3,3,5), (3,4,4): 1/5184, 1/9072, 1/10080, 1/22680; H=5: 1/158400, 1/285120, 1/332640, 1/798336, 1/997920. sign_htk: H=0,3: +; H=1,5: -; H=2: -,+; H=4: +,-,+,-. Item (b), T=0 at z=0. K[C3](lambda;0) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} c0 Q(Lbar) with c0 = prod_P (H-n_P)! / ((H+1)! prod_P (n_P-1)!) and Lbar = sum_v mu_v lambda_v, where mu_N = 1, mu_N' = 0, mu_{P_k} = (n_P-k)/n_P. Lemma: the polarization of Q vanishes on span(Lambda_P) x span(Lambda_P) for each P, so <Q(L)> = Q(<L>) and the covariances of the order statistics sigma^P_k drop out; <sigma^P_k> = (n_P-k)/n_P. Examples: H=2 (1,2,2): K_htk = -(1/6)[Lbar B1][Lbar C1], Lbar = N + B1/2 + C1/2. H=3 (1,3,3): -(1/48)[Lbar B1 B2][Lbar C1 C2], Lbar = N + (2/3)B1 + (1/3)B2 + (2/3)C1 + (1/3)C2. sgn det[B^T; C3] = (-1)^{q+1}, hence K_htk = (-1)^{(q+1)D} K[C3]. Derivation: take the tree E \ {A_1, C_1}, so C_T = (A-B, C-B) = diag(1,-1) C3. Then det B_T = (-1)^{p-1} (block bidiagonal after moving column N past the p-1 A-columns), eps_T = (-1)^{(N-2)+(r-1)}, sigma_T = (-1)^q, and det[B^T; C_T] = sigma_T x (number of trees) (CONVENTIONS Section 1). Root at an interior vertex rho (so N' carries a source). Derivation: y_e = sum_v R_ev(t) lambda_v with R = t^{-1}B(B^T t^{-1}B)^{-1}, and R is scale invariant. K = sigma_T^H eps(n,H) * integral of wedge_r d^H y_{c_r}, with eps(n,H) = (-1)^{nH + C(n,2)C(H,2)} and sigma_T = eps_T det B_T. Each factor expands as d^H y_c = wedge_i (sum_v lambda^i_v dR_cv) = sum_{|S|=H} [lambda_S] dR_{c,S}, so wedge_r d^H y_{c_r} = sum_S prod_r [lambda_{S_r}] * wedge_r dR_{c_r,S_r}. The coefficient forms are absolutely integrable: interpolate at points lambda^(k) whose Vandermonde matrix in the monomials is invertible, then use a left inverse onto the span V_n of products of minors. Consequences: degree exactly n in each component lambda^(i); K(g lambda) = det(g)^n K(lambda); K is a homogeneous polynomial of degree n in the HxH minors of the source matrix.

hCS on C^3 (H=3): every vertex has internal degree >= 2 (from 2(|I|-d) <= 3(|V|-1)-4), so there are four distinct external vertices with momenta p_i and sum p = 0. With p4 = -p1-p2-p3: [124] = -Delta, [134] = Delta, [234] = -Delta, Delta = det(p1,p2,p3), so by (a) K_Gamma = kappa_Gamma Delta^n. Then O_n = c_n * integral of Omega Delta(d1,d2,d3)^n K_abcd A^a A^b A^c A^d with K = sum_Gamma kappa_Gamma W^Gamma / |Aut Gamma|. Each W^Gamma has one f_abc = kappa([X_a,X_b],X_c) per vertex and one kappa^{-1} per edge. Modulo total derivatives, Delta(d_{s1},d_{s2},d_{s3}) = sgn(s) Delta. The fields have total degree 1, so F_n[K] = sgn(s)^{n+1} F_n[K^s], hence F_n[K] = F_n[Pi_n K] with Pi_n = (1/24) sum_s sgn(s)^{n+1} s. Only the totally antisymmetric part (n even) or totally symmetric part (n odd) contributes.

Even n, g reductive, g = z + s with s = [g,g]. (1) f vanishes whenever any slot is central. (2) kappa(z, s) = kappa(z, [s,s]) = kappa([z,s], s) = 0, so kappa^{-1} is block diagonal. (3) Hence W^Gamma vanishes on z and is s-invariant. (4) Pi_even K lies in (Lambda^4 s*)^s. (5) (Lambda^k s*)^s = H^k(s) (Chevalley-Eilenberg, Koszul), and H^4(s) = 0 (Hopf: exterior algebra on odd generators of degree >= 3). So O_even = 0. For g with centre, (Lambda^4 g*)^g = Lambda^4 z* + z* (x) H^3(s) is nonzero, but K has no component there. Assumption: the n-loop graphs contain only the classical cubic vertex, i.e. no local counterterms at loop orders < n.

claims.statement: Chain elimination: t_{E,j} = R_E x_{E,j}, s_{E,k} = Σ_{j>k} x_{E,j}. Sources: μ_p += Σ_k s_{E,k} λ_{E,k}, μ_q += Σ_k (1-s_{E,k}) λ_{E,k}. Currents: y_{E,j} = Y_E - m̂_E + Q_{E,j}. Sourced star-triangle chart at a K4 vertex Dc (S1 Appendix 'Star--triangle reduction with a source'): conductances g_v (Σg=1) and h_v = g_w g_x r_v/(1-r_v); p_v = (1-r_v) g_v, Q = Σ p_v; μ'_v = μ_v + g_v μ_Dc; Y_XY = (p_Y μ'_X - p_X μ'_Y)/Q. Original triangle edge X→Y carries r_Z Y_XY; star edge Dc→v carries g_v μ_Dc - Σ_{w≠v} (1-r_{Z(vw)}) Y_vw. All currents are polynomial in (s, g, r) divided by Q.

Density of K = ∫ D ι_E vol in the coordinates ξ = (s, gA, gB, rA, rB, rC): g(ξ) = s_Γ det[[Q, ∂Q], [N, ∂N]] / Q^10, where N = Q·y over the first edges of the chains on the triangle K4 edges, and s_Γ = ±1 is constant for each graph and center. Then K = s_Γ ∫_{Δ^2×(0,1)^3} P/Q^10, where P is the exact integral of the determinant over s.

Homogenize P to degree Dg = max(deg_g P, 7) with G = Σ g; b = Dg - 7. If b = 0: Feynman formula ∫_{Δ^2} g^β/(ρ·g)^10 = β!/9! ∏ ρ_v^{-β_v-1}, ρ = 1-r. If b > 0: 1/(Q^10 G^b) = Γ(10+b)/(Γ(10)Γ(b)) ∫_0^1 ξ^9 (1-ξ)^{b-1} (Σ_v (1-ξ r_v) g_v)^{-10-b} dξ; the r-integrals then factor into φ(γ,m) = ∫_0^1 r^γ (1-ξr)^{-m} dr. claims.statement: Berezin form: rho_n(M) = pi^{-n/2} int d^n theta d^n a exp(-sum_e t_e Ahat_e^2), with A = C^T a, Theta = C^T theta, Ahat_e = A_e + (dt_e/2t_e) Theta_e and int d^n theta theta_1...theta_n = 1. Derivation: int d^n a e^{-a^T M a + J^T a} = pi^{n/2} (det M)^{-1/2} e^{J^T M^{-1} J/4}. With J = -dM theta, J^T M^{-1} J/4 = (1/2) theta^T A theta, where A = -(1/2) dM M^{-1} dM. Then int d^n theta e^{theta^T A theta/2} = Pf A. Finally a^T M a + a^T dM theta = sum_e (t_e A_e^2 + dt_e A_e Theta_e) = sum_e t_e Ahat_e^2.

Series: the edges of a chain share (A, Theta), and sum_j t_j Ahat_j^2 = R Ahat_R^2 with R = sum_j t_j. So rho_n depends on the times of a chain only through R. In ratio coordinates (t_{m,i,j} = x_{m,i,j} t_m / w_{m,i}), the x_{m,i,j} enter rho_n only through the insertions carried by reduced (loop-containing) edges of that chain.

Exact recursion over the moves m = 1, 2, ... of a series-parallel plan; move m merges chains i = 1..k with R_i = t_m/w_{m,i}. Edge factor exp(-t A^2 - dt A Theta) times an insertion I_e(A, Theta): I_e = 1 for an original edge, polynomial in A and linear in Theta otherwise. Variables: A_i = w_i J + j_i, Theta_i = w_i Theta + vartheta_i, with sum_i j_i = sum_i vartheta_i = 0. Rule: I_m(J,Theta) = (1 + dt_m J Theta) < int d^{k-1} vartheta prod_{i=1}^k (1 - dR_i A_i Theta_i) prod_{e consumed} I_e(s_e A_i, s_e Theta_i) >_j. Here <j_a j_b> = (w_a delta_ab - w_a w_b)/(2 t_m); dR_i = sum_{e in chain i} dt_e; dt_m = sum_i w_i^2 dR_i; dt_e = t_e dlog t_e, with dlog t_e = dlog t_m - dlog w_{m,i} + dlog x_{m,i,j}. The consumed insertions multiply in creation order; the sign of moving them past the unconsumed odd ones is tracked; s_e = +-1 is the orientation of edge e in its chain. Result: rho_n(C_rec) = U^{-1/2} I_final(0,0), with U = prod_m t_m^{k_m-1} prod_i w_{m,i}^{-1} and t_m = prod over ancestors of x/w. C_rec: loop (m,a) = chain a minus chain k, rows ordered by decreasing m.

Closed form for a merge of k plain branches: I_k(J,Theta) = s_k t^{k-1} (prod_{i=1}^k w_i)^{-1} dw_1^...^dw_{k-1} :Jhat^{k-1}:_t. Here :X^p:_t = (2t)^{-p/2} He_p(sqrt(2t) X) (Wick power for variance 1/2t), Jhat = J + (dt/2t) Theta, s_k = (-1)^{(k-1)(k-2)/2}. At J = Theta = 0 by Wick: int d vartheta gives (-1)^{binom(k-1,2)} t^{k-1} e_{k-1}(j_1/w_1^2, ..., j_k/w_k^2) d^{k-1}w, and E[e_{2m}] = (2m-1)!! (-1/2t)^m / prod w_i.

Product formula for bananas (n+1 chains, n even): rho_n = ((n-1)!!/2^{n/2}) prod_{i=1}^{n+1} w_i^{-1/2} dw_1^...^dw_n for C_rec, int over the simplex = pi^{n/2}, and rho_odd = 0. Kernel at (H,1): K_banana(lambda;0) = ((n-1)!!/2^{n/2}) D_Gamma prod_P Gamma(H+3/2-a_P)/(a_P-1)! / Gamma(H+(n+1)/2). D_Gamma is the determinant of the fibre forms: rows (i,a), a < n+1; columns the interior sources of each chain P in path order; entry +lambda for P = a, -lambda for P = n+1. At n=2 this is the theta formula of CONVENTIONS.md. Series compositions of loop-carrying subnetworks break the product structure; see a6.

(1.5): phi_{D_3} = (1/2pi)(a1 da2^da3 - a2 da1^da3 + a3 da1^da2)/(a1a2+a2a3+a1a3)^{3/2}. Also (det M)^{-1/2} Pf(-1/2 dM M^{-1} dM) = eq-rho2 identically.

The integral of phi_{D_3} over the simplex is 1, so the integral of rho_2(D_3) over RP^2_{>0} is pi. This matches BHP I_{D_3}(1) = 1 and, in GKW/BH normalization, I_{D_3} = 2^{-2} = 1/4, which is the S3 remark after Cor. cor-odd.

For every even n: rho_n(M) = (-1/2)^{n/2} phi^{BHP}_M = pi^{n/2} phi^{BH}_G with Lambda_C = M, and therefore rho_n = +-(2 sqrt(pi))^n alpha^{BH}_G. alpha^{BH} uses the GKW normalization, with pi^{-1/2} per edge. S3's M = C t C^T is BHP/BH's dual (cycle) Laplacian Lambda_C = C^T D C.

Balduf-Hu, arXiv:2503.09558, 'The Topological form is the Pfaffian form' (12 Mar 2025). Thm 1 (Sec. 1.1): alpha_G = det(C|P) 2^{-l} phi_G with det(C|P) = +-1. Def. 2 (Sec. 1.3): phi_G = (-2pi)^{-l/2} Pf(dLambda Lambda^{-1} dLambda)/sqrt(det Lambda), Lambda = C^T D C, and det Lambda = psi_G (Lemma 7). Lemma 3(ii): phi_G = 0 for odd l. Cor. 4(iv): alpha^alpha = 0 for non-trees. Sec. 2.2: integral of phi_{D_{2i+1}} = 1 and I_{D_{2i+1}} = 2^{-2i}. Thm 2 (Sec. 3.5): phi_G is a sum over spanning trees. Sec. 2.4 announces a future description of the holomorphic form rho_G in terms of graph matrices; it is not in INSPIRE's author list as of 2026-11-20. INSPIRE lists only 2408.03192 as citing it; Semantic Scholar lists 2611.23377 and 2605.24695. S1, S2 and S3 do not cite 2503.09558 or 2406.12734 (grep).

Brown-Hu-Panzer, arXiv:2406.12734 (v2 9 Jul 2026). Def. 2.1, eq. (2.6): phi_X = det(X)^{-1/2} Pf(dX X^{-1} dX) on positive definite matrices, applied to the dual Laplacian of graphs. Eq. (2.12): phi_X = Q(X)/(det X)^{n+1/2}. Thm 1.3, eq. (1.9): I_G(omega) = (-2pi)^{-l/2} times the integral over sigma_G of omega_G ^ phi_G. I_{D_3}(1) = 1, and I_G(1) = +-1 iff G is the dipole D_{2k+1}. Lemma 2.4, eq. (2.8), dipole pullback: Lambda^* phi^{2i} = (-1)^i ((2i)!/(2^i i!)) (x1...x_{2i+1})^{i-1} S_{2i}(x)^{-i-1/2} Omega_{2i+1}. Integrals with canonical forms give zeta(3), Li_4(1/2) and Catalan's constant (Thm 1.7). No holomorphic factors appear.

Balduf-Gaiotto, arXiv:2408.03192 v2. Eq. (4.7), L even: alpha_Gamma = pi^{(|V|-1)/2} / (2^{L+|E|} (L/2)! prod_e a_e psi^{(L+1)/2}) * (sum (-1)^{i+j} psi^{jk} d_j d_k)^{L/2} W_Gamma. Thm 1 (Sec. 4.3): sum over spanning trees T of det(I[T]) times a sum over permutations of products of edge Dodgson polynomials psi^{sigma(e_i),sigma(e_{i+1})}, with (L-1)!! distinct summands (eq. 4.12). Example 13: explicit dunce's-cap 2-form with denominator 8 psi^{3/2}. Lemma 4: alpha = 0 for odd L. Thm 2: alpha^alpha = 0 for non-trees. The word Pfaffian was not seen in the extracted text, and no integrated values are given.

GKW arXiv:2403.13049, read in TeX source. eq:globalconstraint: n|Gamma_0| = (n-1)|Gamma_1| + n + 1, and locally n|Gamma[S]_0| >= (n-1)|Gamma[S]_1| + n + 1, with n = H+T. This is the counting of the task. In sec:projective, eq:omegafactorize: omega_Gamma = alpha^T prod_i rho_Gamma[lambda^i; z^i] with alpha_Gamma = int prod_e pi^{-1/2} e^{-s_e^2} ds_e. alpha = +-1 on trees and alpha = 0 for odd loop number. The bitriangle alpha is given explicitly (prefactor 1/(8pi) U^{-3/2}), and alpha^2 = 0 is observed. At H = T = 1 the bitriangle density is omega = -(pi^2/4) U^{-5/2} (t12 t23 t31 t24 t43) e^{-lambda A^{-1} B z} lambda_1(lambda_1+lambda_2+lambda_3) dVol_t. No integrated value is given. The Introduction notes there is no non-renormalization theorem for T = 1. In sec:exampleH0T1, I_N = 2^{1-N} for odd N.

Operatope paper arXiv:2207.14321, subsection 'Three-Dimensional Holomorphic-Topological (HT) Twist': omega^{3d}_Gamma = rho(lambda) ^ eta. It vanishes for odd loop number and is nontrivial for even loop number; no values are given. Subsection 'Further Generalizations' gives the (H+T) counting. The 2d B-twist subsection has omega^{2d} = eta ^ eta, observed to vanish at the first few loop orders.

Wang-Williams arXiv:2407.08667 (v3 13 Apr 2026). Abstract: for d'=1 the odd-loop obstructions vanish; for d'>1 all obstructions vanish. Thm 1.1: UV finite. Thm 1.2: for d'=1 the theory is quantized only modulo hbar^2. Prop. 3.21: non-Laman graphs give O = 0. Prop. 3.23: odd h_1 gives O = 0 (reflection). Prop. 3.26 / Lemma 3.24: d' >= 2 gives O = 0. Sec. 1 expects a two-loop anomaly for topological-holomorphic CS on R x C^2 with Lie algebra g; it is not computed. No Pfaffian appears, only a det(M_Gamma)^{-(d+d'/2)} asymptotic prefactor.

Loop computations found for one topological direction. 11d sugra on R x C^5: one loop only (RSW 2111.03049 Sec. 1.6, Thm 1.4; higher orders deferred; J produces graphs at all loop orders). 5d CS: one loop only (Costello 1705.02500 Sec. 9.3, Prop. 9.3.1, normalization 2^5 pi^2; Oh-Zhou 2002.07343 abstract). Costello 1610.04144: Sec. 9.1 places anomalies in H^3(X) and H^1(X); Thm 9.0.2 gives no obstructions on C^2 for the non-commutative theory; negative powers of epsilon are admitted to cancel potential higher-loop anomalies. 3d HT: Garner-Williams-Balduf 2611.23377 (17 Nov 2026), App. A, one loop: level k - hbar h^vee (A.26), c -> c + 13 hbar, I_DD = 1/(4 pi i) (A.46). Its Sec. 2.3.2 gives power hbar^{E-V} with E <= V+2; composites need not stop at hbar^2. Costello-Dimofte-Gaiotto 2005.00083 Sec. 1.2: Kac-Moody level k-h. Dimofte-Niu-Py 2508.11749 Sec. 1: interacting 3d HT theories carry higher A-infinity operations; Prop. 6.1: tree-level exactness for quasi-linear theories. Gwilliam-Rabinovich-Williams 2107.06734 Sec. 1: mixed BF on R^m x C^n with m>0 is one-loop exact, with no higher-loop diagrams. None of these papers gives a closed form at two loops or more with H >= 1.

Twists of maximal SYM. Elliott-Safronov-Williams 2002.10517: 10d hCS on C^5 (4.1.1); 9d CS type on C^4 x R (5.1.1); 8d holomorphic BF on C^4 (6.1.1); 7d generalized BF on C^3 x R (7.1.1); 6d holomorphic BF plus symplectic boson on C^3 (8.1.1); 5d generalized BF plus symplectic boson on C^2 x R (9.1.1); 4d and 3d BF plus R-matter (10.1.1, 11.1.1). That text uses no odd coordinates. Eager-Saberi 1805.02084, Sec. 8, eq. (8.2), citing Costello: the twist of maximal SYM in 2k dimensions has fields Omega^{0,*}(C^k) (x) C[psi_1..psi_{5-k}] (x) u(N), with odd psi. Odd-dimensional R x C^k reductions are not treated in that section.

Costello-Li 1905.09269. Sec. II.5 and III.2: one-loop box anomaly on C^3, cancelled iff Tr_ad X^4 is proportional to (Tr_fun X^2)^2; for so_n, Tr_ad X^4 = (n-8) Tr_fun X^4 + 3 (Tr_fun X^2)^2, so SO(8). Sec. III.3 argues anomalies vanish beyond one loop by counting the dimensions of possible counterterms in the coupled open-closed theory; no two-loop computation. Costello-Li 1505.06703 Sec. 1 and 1.9: the one-loop anomaly alpha_1/2 + alpha_2 is double-trace and is cancelled by the closed sector; the coupled theory with gl(N) cannot be quantized. No statement was found about the n >= 2 anomaly of hCS alone with simple g.

O1, T=1 two-loop theta kernels (D_theta/2) prod_P Gamma(H+3/2-n_P)/(n_P-1)!/Gamma(H+3/2). PARTIALLY KNOWN. rho_2 on theta graphs as a Pfaffian form is known (BHP Def. 2.1; BH Def. 2, eq. (1.5); BG Thm 1). The H=0 value is known (BHP Thm 1.3, I_{D_3}(1) = 1; BH Sec. 2.2; GKW I_3 = 1/4) and agrees with an integral of rho_2 equal to pi (chk-intphi). NOT FOUND: the closed form for H >= 1; c_166 = 1/158400 at H=5; pi/3 for the (1,1) bitriangle (GKW gives only the integrand); pi/20 and pi/30 at (2,1).

O2, hCS on C^3: the n-loop obstruction with cubic vertices has 4 legs and kernel c_n Delta^n; even n pairs with Lambda^4(g)^g, and H^4(g) = 0. KNOWN only for n=1 (box with Tr_ad X^4, Costello-Li 1905.09269 Sec. II.5, III.2). NOT FOUND for n >= 2 with hCS alone and simple g. Higher loops appear only in the coupled open-closed theory, through a dimension count (1905.09269 Sec. III.3; 1505.06703 Sec. 1.8-1.9).

O3, maximal SYM twists as hCS on C^{H|k} x R^T with H+T+k=5. Even D: KNOWN (Eager-Saberi 1805.02084 Sec. 8, eq. 8.2). Odd D on C^H x R: PARTIALLY KNOWN in CS/BF/matter form (ESW 5.1.1, 7.1.1, 9.1.1, 11.1.1). The uniform odd-coordinate presentation with T=1: NOT FOUND. D=8 and D=7 are of BF type (ESW 6.1.1, 7.1.1), and mixed BF with m>0 has no bulk diagrams beyond one loop (GRW 2107.06734 Sec. 1). Q_odd = 0 for odd D: KNOWN (GKW sec:projective; WW abstract and Prop. 3.23; BG Lemma 4; BH Lemma 3(ii); operatope 3d HT subsection). Q_2 graphs are theta graphs with O at a trivalent vertex: the counting is KNOWN (GKW eq:globalconstraint with n = D); the theta-graph statement itself was NOT FOUND.

C1, closed-form evaluation of two-loop or higher graph integrals with one topological direction and H >= 1 (3d N=2 HT, 5d CS / twisted M-theory, twisted 11d sugra): NOT FOUND. Only the following were found: integrands (GKW bitriangle; operatope 3d HT), one-loop values (2611.23377 App. A; 1705.02500 Prop. 9.3.1; 2002.07343), H=0 dipoles (GKW, BH, BHP), and H=0 canonical-form integrals (BHP Thm 1.7).

C2, loop corrections to the BRST differential or supercharge in twisted 3d N=2/4/8, 5d N=1/2, 6d N=(1,1), 7d or 8d SYM: NOT FOUND. Related work: ABJM one-loop supercharge outside the twist/graph-integral formalism (Behan-Pipolo de Gioia 2512.23603 [INSPIRE abstract]; Belin-Singh-Vadala-Zaffaroni 2512.04146 [abs]); 3d HT one-loop level shifts (2005.00083; 2611.23377). Budzik-Kulp 2512.07771 (TeX) computes only 4d and says the formalism extends to other dimensions. The 2026 citers of 2512.07771 work in 4d N=4, ABJM or BMN matrix QM, not twisted D != 4 SYM.

C3. Two-loop anomaly of hCS on C^3: NOT FOUND (only the one-loop anomaly is known, see lit-hCS-C3). Two-loop anomaly of topological-holomorphic CS on R x C^2: PARTIALLY KNOWN. Wang-Williams 2407.08667 Sec. 1 expects it but does not compute it; odd loops vanish (Prop. 3.23); for d'=1 quantization holds only modulo hbar^2 (Thm 1.2). Costello 1610.04144 Thm 9.0.2 and Sec. 9.1 show the non-commutative deformation is unobstructed.

It is not in the BG text read, but is in Balduf-Hu 2503.09558 Thm 1 with Def. 2 and Brown-Hu-Panzer 2406.12734 Def. 2.1: alpha_G = +-2^{-l} (-2pi)^{-l/2} (det Lambda)^{-1/2} Pf(dLambda Lambda^{-1} dLambda), Lambda = C^T diag(a) C. S3's rho_n(M) equals pi^{n/2} phi^{BH}_G (chk-rho2 at n=2; rho-n-general).

C5, raviolo vertex algebras and higher brackets: KNOWN as structures. Garner-Williams 2308.04414; Alfonsi-Kim-Young 2401.11917; Oh-Yagi 1908.05791 (shifted PVAs in topological-holomorphic sectors); Khan-Zeng 2502.13227 (classical); Alfonsi-Kim 2502.05077 (free theories); Chen-Liniado 2507.01858; GKW p-brackets; Dimofte-Niu-Py 2508.11749 Prop. 6.1 (tree level). directions.headline: {I^{x12}}_0 of the 11d action (S3): no graph at g^0 (zero identically). No (a) vertex beta d mu survives D_theta, so all 13 edges are mu->gamma and every sector at g^m is mu^{11-2m} gamma^{2m-1} nu^K with 1<=m<=5, 10+K fields and 22+m derivatives. Each theta graph has 4*binom(10,2m-1) admissible flows at g^m (40,480,1008,480,40). For the smallest sector, g^1 mu^9 gamma with 23 derivatives, I wrote out the kernel/vertex-tensor formula: 200 flows with 12288 letter maps each. Its pieces pass exact pointwise checks against brute-force Kirchhoff currents. Part (c), whether that sector vanishes or is Q_0-exact, was not done: the jet basis has 63,414,968,175,297,950 monomials.

claims.statement: g^0 part vanishes identically. With m vertices of type (c), n_a of type (a) and n_b of type (b_k), n_a+n_b+m=12. Types (a) and (b_k) have one incoming (gamma or beta) leg each, (c) has three, so there are 12+2m incoming legs. Every one of the |I|=13 edges uses one, so m>=1 (S3 lem-g with in(O)=1 or 3).

No vertex of type (a) beta d_i mu^i appears in any nonzero contribution. Hence no beta letter, no nu-beta edge, all 13 edges are mu->gamma and every nu is external. Reason: D_theta is an overall factor of K_theta[F] (S3 eq-insertion) and is linear in lambda_v for each interior vertex v, so every interior vertex needs an external letter. (a) has two letters, so it can be neither trivalent nor interior.

Sectors at order g^m: external content mu^{11-2m} gamma^{2m-1} nu^K, with m=1..5 and K = sum_v k_v >= 0. Number of external fields is 10+K. Number of derivatives is (12+m)+10 = 22+m. Number of epsilons is 2+m. Parity is odd. At K=0 each of the 10 interior vertices carries exactly one external letter and N, N' carry none, so lambda_N = lambda_N' = 0.

Vertex roles by flow in/out degree. Interior: (1,1) is b_k with external mu nu^k; (0,2) is a b_k source with external gamma nu^k; (2,0) is a (c) sink with external gamma. Trivalent: (1,2) is b_k with external nu^k; (3,0) is (c) with nothing external. (0,3) and (2,1) are excluded. Each theta_pqr has 2048 = 2^11 admissible flows; at order g^m there are 4*binom(10,2m-1) = 40, 480, 1008, 480, 40, the same for all five graphs. At m=1: 20 flows have (c) as an interior sink (the path through the sink is directed into it from N and N', and the other two paths form a directed cycle); 20 have (c) at N or N' with one interior b_0 source carrying the external gamma.

Reduced theta density at T=1, H=5: D(t)|det[t; dt/dxi]| = -(D_theta/2) prod_P w_P^{11/2-n_P}, i.e. K^S3 = -K^htk, which confirms the sign of S3 eq-Ktheta. The polynomial currents agree with the Kirchhoff solution exactly.

Jet basis of the g^1 mu^9 gamma sector (9 distinct odd mu jets and one gamma jet, 23 derivatives, torus weight (3,3,3,3,3)) has 63,414,968,175,297,950 monomials, counted before the quotient by total derivatives.
Whether the g^1 mu^9 gamma sector vanishes, or is Q_0-exact, modulo total derivatives.

Space of counterterms needed for the Q_0-exactness test at order g in this sector: J = J_1[mu^8 gamma] + J_2[mu^8 nu gamma] + J_3[mu^7 beta], 22 derivatives each. Only Q_0 at order g^0 contributes, and it preserves N_{gamma beta}. Q_0-closedness of the order-g obstruction follows from the vanishing at g^0.

Part (c) is new. It is the two-loop obstruction of topological-holomorphic CS on R x C^2 (D=3, T=1). WW 2407.08667 Sec. 1 only expects a two-loop anomaly, and their Thm 1.2 quantizes only mod hbar^2. None of the 14 INSPIRE citers of WW computes it, and web searches found no computation.
Verified (c1, c4-c8, with exact ranks and a formal-in-N argument): K_133 = -(pi/20)[p1p2][p3p4] and K_223 = (pi/30)[p1p2][p3p4]; each graph is closed; O_2 is exact for sl2, gl2; it is non-exact for sl_N, gl_N with N>=3; F_133+F_223 is exact. The exact sl2/gl2 result partly answers WW's expectation (O_2 is a coboundary there, so it can be removed by a counterterm).
Non-exactness does not depend on the unverified relative Wick sign (c3). The unverified constant hbar^2/(64 pi^5) (c2) affects only the coefficient.
Penalties: (a) is immediate from y_e linear in lambda (polynomiality, det^n covariance). (b) is a short consequence of H^4(s)=0. It rests on a no-counterterm assumption that hCS on C^3 alone violates, because the one-loop box is nonzero and non-exact (b4; Costello-Li 1905.09269). The identification of local cohomology with CE cochains of g[[z1,z2]] modulo translations is argued, not taken from a source.

I found no holomorphic or HT graph kernel with a transcendental value in the literature. The operatope paper (2207.14321) says its quadratic relations 'appear to fully determine' the integrals. BHP 2406.12734 has zeta(3) only for H=0 canonical-form integrals. S1 has rational moments only for source-free star-triangle moves.
New here: zeta(3) in four of the six K4 subdivisions on C^3 at n=3, and in 8 of the 10 nonzero coefficients of the four-source C^2 prism at n=4. The C^2 case lies inside the 4d holomorphic twist.
Verification: independent reduction-free numerics reproduce every value to relative 1e-7 (2e-8 for one). The exact closed forms come from a Mathematica pipeline; its P->H step (a2) was not reproduced independently, so the identification of zeta(3), and hence irrationality, rests on it. It is supported by 66-102 digit agreement of two quadratures of the exported 1D integrand.
Other items: b4 refuted (K33 four-source value is 6.32e-5, not 6.4e-5). b6, c2, c3 unverified.

The verified material is only a sector classification of {I^{x12}}_0: no g^0 term, no beta-d-mu vertex, 4 binom(10,2m-1) flows, and the jet count 6.34e16. Whether the obstruction vanishes or is exact (c1) is open. The two-loop quantum master equation of twisted 11d sugra (RSW 2111.03049) is therefore not settled.

A literature survey, with no research claim. Its exact check rho_2(Lambda(D_3)) = pi phi_{D_3}, together with BH Thm 1 and BHP Def. 2.1, shows that the S3 factor rho_n(M) = det(M)^{-1/2} Pf(-1/2 dM M^{-1} dM) is already published. This lowers every candidate that presents rho_n as new.

judges.flagship_title: Holomorphic-topological Feynman integrals on R^T x C^H: theta and fan kernels, zeta(3) beyond series-parallel networks, and the two-loop anomaly of five-dimensional Chern-Simons theory
flagship_statements:
Theorem 2 (theta kernels, T=0, all H >= 1).
D(t) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} R_A R_B R_C Q(L(t))/U^{H+2}.
K[C3](lambda;0) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} [prod_P (H-n_P)! / ((H+1)! prod_P (n_P-1)!)] Q(Lbar).
Here Lbar = lambda_N + sum_{P,k} ((n_P-k)/n_P) lambda^P_k.
Lemma used: the symmetric bilinear form of Q vanishes on span(Lambda_P) x span(Lambda_P) for each P, so E[Q(L)] = Q(E[L]).
Positive basis: K = (-1)^{H(q+1)} K[C3].
Examples:
- H=2, (1,2,2): K = -(1/6)[Lbar B1][Lbar C1];
- H=3, (1,3,3): -(1/48)[Lbar B1 B2][Lbar C1 C2];
- H=3, (2,2,3): +(1/48)[Lbar A1 B1][Lbar C1 C2].
General sources at the trivalent vertex of the 6d graphs: I_A = (1/432)(3<123>+2<124>+<125>)(<145>+2<245>+3<345>) and I_B = -(1/288)(3<uwq>+2<uwa>+<uwb>)(2<qab>+<uab>+<wab>).
Proved; checked exactly on all 16 tight graphs with H <= 6.

Lemma 4 (Gaussian sources at (H,T) = (1,1), any graph).
Let Lambda be the grounded Kirchhoff conductance matrix and kappa ~ N(0, Lambda/2). Then
U^{-1} rho_n wedge prod_r psi_r[lambda] = U^{1/2} E_kappa[ U^{-2} prod_r psi_r[kappa] wedge prod_r psi_r[lambda] ].
The right-hand side is U^{1/2} times the (H,T) = (2,0) integrand with the two holomorphic source components (kappa, lambda).
Exact Wick check on fans with n = 2, 4 and on three non-fan graphs.

Theorem 5 (fans at (H,T) = (1,1), all loops).
Fan: path vertices 1..n+1 and root O; a_i = (i,i+1), b_i = (i,O); edge order a_1,b_1,...,a_n,b_n,b_{n+1}; positively oriented cycle basis. K_n = 0 for odd n. For even n:
(i) Endpoint sources (lambda_2 = ... = lambda_n = 0): K_n(lambda;0) = (4 pi lambda_1 lambda_{n+1})^{n/2}/((n+1)(n!)^2). For n = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 this gives pi/3, pi^2/180, pi^3/56700, pi^4/57153600, pi^5/141455160000, each times (lambda_1 lambda_{n+1})^{n/2}.
(ii) General sources: K_n = ((4 pi)^{n/2}/((n+1)(n!)^2)) E[Haf_n(l,m)]/(n-1)!!. The ensemble has independent u_m ~ Beta((n+1-m)/2,1) (m<n), v_k ~ Beta(3/2,k/2) (k<n), and (u_n, v_n, 1-u_n-v_n) ~ Dir(1/2, n/2, 1). The entries are
- l_i = lambda^red_i/P_i;
- m_j = lambda_{n+1} + v_n^{-1} sum_{k>j} (1-u_k) lambda^{(j)}_k / prod_{m=k}^{n-1}(1-v_m);
- lambda^{(j)}_k = sum_{w=j+1}^k (P_k/P_w) lambda_w.
Hence K_n is in lambda_1 lambda_{n+1} pi^{n/2} Q[lambda].
(iii) Sources (lambda_1, lambda_2, 0, ..., 0, lambda_{n+1}): K_n = ((4 pi)^{n/2}/((n+1)(n!)^2)) lambda_{n+1}^{n/2} [(lambda_1+lambda_2)^{n/2} - lambda_2^{n/2}].
(iv) Low orders: K_2 = (pi/3) lambda_1 lambda_3 and K_4 = (pi^2/180) lambda_1 lambda_5 [(lambda_1+2lambda_2+2lambda_3)(2lambda_3+2lambda_4+lambda_5) + 8 lambda_3^2].
(v) Reflection symmetry: K_n(lambda_1..lambda_{n+1}) = K_n(lambda_{n+1}..lambda_1).
(vi) Endpoint Taylor expansion in z: all orders are given by the factorial ratio c^{(n)}. Its prefactor is (n-1)!!/2^{n/2} Gamma(1/2+sum_i r_in) Gamma(n/2+sum_i s_i)/Gamma((n+3)/2+sum r_in+sum s_i) prod_{j<n} 2/(n+1-j+2X_j); the remaining Beta factors and the full statement are in fans-ht claim b1, with X_j, Y_j as in S1 eq-sum-N4-coeff.
(vii) (2,0) control: K^{(2,0)}_n = (-1)^{n(n+1)/2} det(lambda_1,lambda_{n+1})^n/((n!)^3(n+1)), as in S1.

Proposition 6 (powers of pi at T=1 for series-parallel graphs; one vanishing).
(i) In the ratio coordinates of any series-parallel plan, U = prod_m t_m^{k_m-1} prod_i w_{m,i}^{-1}.
(ii) Hypothesis: every leading ratio exponent of the reduced density is > -1. Under it, K(lambda;0) is in pi^{ceil(n/2)+2E} Q[lambda], with E = sum over chains of floor(#{odd-loop edges in the chain}/2). In particular E = 0 implies K(lambda;0) in pi^{n/2} Q[lambda]. The hypothesis is observed (exponents >= -1/2) in all computed cases but not proved.
(iii) Graph [2,2,2,4,4,4] at (H,T) = (1,1), edges (0,1)(0,2)(0,4)(0,5)(1,2)(1,3)(1,4)(3,4)(4,5); it has E = 1. In C_rec, rho_4 = -(1/2) prod_{m=1}^3 [(w_{m1}w_{m2})^{-1/2} dw_{m1}] wedge d sqrt(Pi), with Pi = t_9 t_10 t_11/(t_9+t_10+t_11)^3. Consequently K_Gamma(lambda;z) = 0 for all lambda and z and for every polynomial current insertion, while the density is nonzero.

Theorem 9 (two-loop anomaly of 5d Chern-Simons theory).
Setting: topological-holomorphic CS theory on R x C^2 with Lie algebra g and nondegenerate invariant form, heat-kernel gauge, no order-hbar local counterterms. The odd-loop obstructions vanish (rho_odd = 0).
The order-hbar^2 obstruction is O_2 = N sum_{Gamma = theta(1,3,3), theta(2,2,3)} |Aut Gamma|^{-1} int Omega K_Gamma(d;0) W^Gamma(A,A,A,A), with |Aut| = 4, 4.
Kernels (engine orientation): K_133 = -(pi/20)[p1p2][p3p4] and K_223 = +(pi/30)[p1p2][p3p4].
For the derived Wick sign: O_2 = (pi N/240) int d^2z [d1d2][d3d4] W_tot, with W_tot = -3W_133 + 2W_223. For sl_2, W_tot = -104 k12k34 + 16 k13k24 + 40 k14k23 with k_ij = tr(A_iA_j).
(i) Each graph gives a BRST-closed functional.
(ii) For g = sl_2, gl_2, O_2 is BRST-exact.
(iii) For g = sl_N, gl_N with N >= 3, F_133 = alt([p1p2][p3p4]W_133) and F_223 are each non-exact, and F_133 + F_223 is exact. Hence [O_2] = (pi N/48)[F_223] != 0. With the opposite relative sign of the two graphs, [O_2] = +-(pi N/240)[F_223] != 0.
Status: N = +-hbar^2/(64 pi^5) is derived only.

Corollary 10 (holomorphic CS on C^3, classical cubic vertex).
n-loop obstruction graphs have four external vertices, and K_Gamma = kappa_Gamma Delta^n, Delta = det(p1,p2,p3). Only the sgn^{n+1}-isotypic part of sum_Gamma kappa_Gamma W^Gamma/|Aut Gamma| contributes.
For reductive g = z + s and even n, this part lies in (Lambda^4 s*)^s = H^4(s) = 0, so the even-loop obstruction from classical-vertex graphs vanishes.
n = 2:
- K_theta(1,3,3) = -(1/432)(2[123]+[124])(2[134]+[234]), which is -Delta^2/432 mod sum p;
- K_theta(2,2,3) = (1/288)(2[123]+[124])([134]+[234]), which is 0 mod sum p;
- Alt W_Gamma = 0.
missing_for_publication: Theorem 9, normalization: an independent derivation of the constant N = +-hbar^2/(64 pi^5) (c2) and of the relative Wick sign between theta(1,3,3) and theta(2,2,3) (c3), for example by a position-space evaluation. The class coefficient pi N/48 depends on both.
Theorem 9, local cohomology: a derivation, or a cited proof, that local BRST cohomology on R x C^2 equals CE cochains of g[[z1,z2]] modulo translations, with the tau direction giving only a shift.

Theorem 9, order-hbar deformations: treat closed local deformations J. Show that {J,J}/2, and any one-loop graph with a J vertex (zero at T=1), cannot cancel [O_2]. State exactly which quantization the theorem refers to (commutative theory, no Moyal deformation).

Theorem 9, comparison with 3d: check whether the analogous two-loop heat-kernel obstruction at (H,T) = (1,1) is Q_0-exact, as one-loop exactness in holomorphic gauge for 3d HT CS requires (Gwilliam-Williams 2111.00955; Garner-Williams-Balduf 2611.23377).

Theorems 7-8: an independent exact derivation of the zeta(3) coefficients. The P->H step (Feynman-parameter formula, r-integrals, final xi-integral, done in Mathematica) has to be reproduced in a second system, or replaced by an analytic derivation. Without it, irrationality rests on one pipeline plus 7-digit numerics.

Theorems 7-8, remaining cases: the exact K_{3,3} four-source value, which needs two nested sourced star-triangle moves (numerical value (6.324 +- 0.005)e-5); the generic five-source prism; and z-Taylor coefficients of the n=4 non-series-parallel kernels.

Theorem 8 versus the operatope paper: implement the quadratic relations of 2207.14321 (eq:II) on the prism. Compute the n<=3 C^2 kernels with insertions, and decide whether zeta(3) refutes the statement that the relations determine the integrals, or forces zeta(3) into lower-loop insertion kernels (b6 unverified).

Theorem 5: verify the K_6 and K_8 polynomials (a10), or drop them. Prove the chart Jacobian formula det[t;dt/dr] = (-1)^{n-1} U^2 prod (1-v_k)^{-1} for general n (proved only for n = 2, 4). Define N(O) in the configuration-sum formula.
Theorems 1-2: write out the sign computations of derivation step (2) and the chart sign (-1)^{q-1}. They are currently asserted and fixed only by pointwise checks.

Proposition 6: prove the exponent hypothesis (all leading ratio exponents > -1), or state the result as conditional. Prove or remove conjecture c5 (E >= 1 implies K = 0); n=6 evidence is QMC at the 1-3% level only.
Corollary 10: fix c_n and the H=3 Koszul sign of W versus K from Feynman rules. State it only as a statement about classical-vertex graphs, since the one-loop box obstruction is non-exact.
Physics context for Theorem 5 and Lemma 4: name the 3d HT observable that the heat-kernel (1,1) fans compute, and its relation to gauge-invariant data.

Write-ups: the derivation chains exist only as structured claims. REPORT.md is missing in every direction. Unify conventions with S1-S3, including the S1 Fig. 3.1 edge-order sign, the S2 eq-B-norm (-1)^n discrepancy, and the I^S2 = -K_htk and K^S3 = -K[C3] dictionary.

Literature: compare BH, BHP, BG, WW and GKW against their TeX sources, not web extractions, and cite them for rho_n, rho^rho = 0, odd-loop vanishing and the H=T=1 bitriangle integrand. Re-check post-2026-11-21 arXiv and math-only papers, which INSPIRE covers incompletely.
risks: Forthcoming overlap: Balduf-Hu (Sec. 2.4) announce a graph-matrix description of the holomorphic form rho_G. A paper on it could cover Theorems 1-2 and Lemma 4.

Theorem 9, scope: non-exactness is robust to the unverified relative sign and constant. Two points remain:
- the local-cohomology identification is argued;
- order-hbar deformations J with {J,J} are not excluded.
The statement concerns the commutative theory. Costello's non-commutative deformation (1610.04144 Thm 9.0.2) is unobstructed. That sl_2 and gl_2 give an exact O_2 contradicts a naive reading of WW's 'two-loop anomaly for a Lie algebra g' and must be stated carefully.

Theorem 9, literature: a computation of the 5d CS two-loop obstruction could exist outside INSPIRE's citers of 2407.08667, for example in the Oh-Zhou or Ishtiaque-Jeong-Zhou line (2002.07343, 2103.00963, 2408.15712), whose two-loop diagrams were only seen as search hits.

Theorems 7-8: the zeta(3) identifications rest on one computer-algebra pipeline. Its P->H step is unreproduced, the independent numerics reach 6-8 digits, and PSLQ was run on the pipeline output. A pipeline error that preserves 7 digits is unlikely but not excluded. Irrationality also depends on Apery's theorem being applicable to the exact value. One related numeric (b4, K33) was refuted at the 1% level.

Theorems 7-8 versus the operatope paper: the result contradicts the expectation in 2207.14321 that the quadratic relations determine all integrals. Referees will require the relations to be checked explicitly on the prism.

Theorem 5 and Lemma 4, physical relevance: in 3d HT Chern-Simons(-matter) theories, holomorphic gauge is one-loop exact (Gwilliam-Williams 2111.00955; Garner-Williams-Balduf 2611.23377). Heat-kernel two-loop fans at (1,1) may therefore carry no gauge-invariant information.
Unproved hypotheses: absolute convergence for every lambda (anomaly-structure a1); exponents > -1 (Proposition 6); a general-n fan Jacobian (Theorem 5).

Dependence on unpublished notes: the H=3 and H=5 parts of Theorem 1 and the twisted-SYM applications (six-d-Q3, msym-odd, msym-D8) build on the unpublished S2 and S3 notes. If those appear separately first, the novelty of these parts shrinks. If they appear later, their own sign discrepancies (S2 eq-B-norm, S3 varsigma) must be resolved first.

Literature coverage: the literature reading was done through web extractions, several of them truncated (BG Sec. 4.3; 2508.11749 Sec. 6; 2107.06734 Secs. 4-5; 2406.12734 beyond 100k characters). Statements attributed to these papers have not been checked against their TeX.

Part (b) proves the RESEARCH_STATE observation (ii): every even-n classical-vertex obstruction of hCS on C^3 vanishes for reductive g, because (Lambda^4 s*)^s = H^4(s) = 0. This is consistent with the dimension-counting argument of Costello-Li 1905.09269 Sec. III.3, but its physical bearing is limited: the one-loop box class is non-exact (b4), so hCS alone is already obstructed and the coupled theory has other vertices. Part (a), polynomiality and det^n covariance of T=0 kernels, is a structural statement about integrals. Without the explicit universal kernels and the MSYM counterpart, the article is narrower than the combined one.

For 8d, Q_1 is the pentagon with <1234>/24 and Q_1^2+{Q_0,Q_2}=0 holds with |k| = 4/|Aut| (su(2)). The best-verified operator-level result of the run. All ten claims are confirmed independently, the order-hbar^3 relation is inhomogeneous, and the solution kappa = (-1/2,1/2,-1,1/8,-1/2) is unique in so(5) and so(6). The all-n statement p<=1 is structural. It extends S2, an unpublished note of the same program, from two to three loops. The physical question it answers is posed only internally (PLAN T2 item 1). The signs are fitted, not derived, and the theory is non-renormalizable.

ranking.rationale: This gives a new structural fact: kernels of graphs that are not series-parallel lie in Q + Q zeta(3) and are not rational in general. Examples are the C^2 prism at four loops (8 of 10 nonzero coefficients) and four of six C^3 K4 subdivisions at three loops. It answers PLAN E6 question 1 ('Is I_Gamma(lambda;0) in Q[lambda]? [open]') in the negative. Physically, the C^3 K4 subdivisions are exactly the n=3 four-leg obstruction graphs of hCS on C^3 (the structure of anomaly-structure b1). Their symmetric part pairs with Sym^4 invariants, so zeta(3) enters the three-loop anomaly kernels relevant to Costello-Li 1905.09269 Sec. III.3 and PLAN T4 item 4, but the anomaly was not assembled. The prism is a four-loop Laman graph of 4d holomorphic theories. The tension with the operatope abstract (4dDiffPaper.tex line 38: quadratic relations 'appear to fully determine the final answer') rests on b6, which is unverified. Deductions: these are only integrals. The zeta(3) closed forms come from the explorer's Mathematica pipeline and are confirmed independently only to 6-8 digits. b4 is refuted. No physical Q_n or quantum-product occurrence of a zeta(3) graph is established (S1 line 128 asserts polynomial currents for renormalizable theories).

Universal closed forms for all two-loop theta kernels at T = 0, 1 and D <= 6, with z-dependence, are fully confirmed. They supply the integrated GKW bitriangle value pi/3 (Higher.tex line 1468, density only) and confirm S3 eq-R-c. They fix the sign of S3 eq-Ktheta and resolve the forms_check.py Monte Carlo discrepancy of S3 (sign convention plus infinite variance). They reproduce S1 eq-1-42, S2 eq-IA/eq-IB with general trivalent sources, and S4 -1/432. Alone this is a set of integrals: H=0 values and the Pfaffian form of rho_n are already published (BH 2503.09558 Thm 1, BHP 2406.12734 Def. 2.1, per novelty-lit, which was read through web extraction and has no verifier). The value lies in the physical applications, which need the other directions.

5d MSYM HT twist: Q_1 = 0, Q_2 is supported on two theta graphs, and the relative coefficient (1,1) is fixed by nilpotency on so(3) and so(5). The 7d coefficients are (-3,6,1) (so(3) only). The 3d single-graph closure is shown. These are new statements about twisted 5d/7d/3d maximal SYM. The closure test is homogeneous because Q_1 = 0, so it fixes only ratios. The prefactor i/128pi^5, the overall sign, raw-normalization and the S2 eq-B-norm (-1)^n comparison are unverified. Whether Q_2 lifts any Q_0-class is not shown.

8d hCS on C^{4|1}: the pentagon Q_1 and the three-theta Q_2 satisfy Q_1^2+{Q_0,Q_2}=0 with |k| = 4/|Aut| (inhomogeneous, but su(2) only). The kernels are confirmed exactly. judges.flagship_title: Universal two-loop kernels of holomorphic-topological theories: the two-loop gauge anomaly of five-dimensional Chern-Simons theory and the first loop correction of twisted maximal super-Yang-Mills
flagship_statements: Setting (twoloop-universal C0, C7). Theta graph theta(p,q,r): trivalent vertices N and N' = root; paths P in {A,B,C} with n_P = p,q,r edges P_1..P_{n_P}, oriented N -> N'; interior vertex P_k carries lambda^P_k; Lambda_P = (lambda^P_1..lambda^P_{n_P-1}) is H x (n_P-1). R_P = sum_j t_{P_j}, U = R_A R_B + R_B R_C + R_C R_A, x^P_j = t_{P_j}/R_P, sigma^P_k = sum_{j>k} x^P_j, w_P = R_P^{-1}/sum_Q R_Q^{-1}. D_theta = det[(Lambda_A;0),(Lambda_B;Lambda_B),(0;Lambda_C)] and Q(v) = det[(v;0),(0;v),(Lambda_A;0),(Lambda_B;Lambda_B),(0;Lambda_C)]. Cycle basis C3 = (A-B, B-C), edge order A,B,C. Then K_htk = (-1)^{(q+1)D} K[C3], I^{S1} = -K_htk (H=2), I^{S2} = -K_htk (H=3), K^{S3} = -K[C3] (H=5, T=1).

Theorem 1 (T = 1 theta kernels; C2, C3, C4, C5). Let H >= 0, p+q+r = 2H+3, n_P <= H+1, with arbitrary sources. Density: D(t) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} D_theta/(2 U^{H+3/2}); it is independent of lambda_N and depends on t only through U. Kernel: K[C3](lambda;z) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} (D_theta/2) int_{Delta^2} d^2w prod_P w_P^{H+1/2-n_P} int_{prod_P Delta^{n_P-1}} dx exp(sum_v lambda_v.X_v), with Z_P = sum_j z_{P_j}, W = sum_P w_P Z_P, X_N = -W, X_{P_k} = sigma^P_k (Z_P - W) - sum_{j>k} z_{P_j}, X_{N'} = 0. At z = 0: K[C3](lambda;0) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2} (D_theta/2) prod_P Gamma(H+3/2-n_P) / (Gamma(H+3/2) prod_P (n_P-1)!). Values of K/(pi D_theta) up to the sign (-1)^{H(H+1)/2}: H=1: 1/3; H=2: 1/20, 1/30; H=3: 1/252, 1/420, 1/840; H=4: 1/5184, 1/9072, 1/10080, 1/22680; H=5: 1/158400, 1/285120, 1/332640, 1/798336, 1/997920. For the (H,T) = (1,1) bitriangle, K_htk = -(pi/3) lambda_B lambda_C. Checks: exact pointwise for all 16 T=1 graphs with D <= 6; direct integration to 12.6-15.9 digits at z = 0 and 13-15 digits at z != 0.

Theorem 2 (T = 0 theta kernels; C2, C6, C10, C11). Let p+q+r = 2H+1, n_P <= H. Density: D(t) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} R_A R_B R_C Q(L(t))/U^{H+2}, with L(t) = lambda_N + sum_{P,k} sigma^P_k lambda^P_k. Kernel: K[C3](lambda;0) = (-1)^{H(H+1)/2+1} [prod_P (H-n_P)! / ((H+1)! prod_P (n_P-1)!)] Q(Lbar), with Lbar = lambda_N + sum_{P,k} ((n_P-k)/n_P) lambda^P_k. This follows because the polarization of Q vanishes on span(Lambda_P) x span(Lambda_P). Special cases: I^{S1}_{fan2} = -(1/24)[lambda_1, lambda_3+2lambda_2][lambda_3, lambda_1+2lambda_2]; I^{S2}_A = (1/432)(3<123>+2<124>+<125>)(<145>+2<245>+3<345>); I^{S2}_B = -(1/288)(3<uwq>+2<uwa>+<uwb>)(2<qab>+<uab>+<wab>).

Theorem 3 (two-loop obstruction of Chern-Simons theory on R x C^2; anomaly-structure c1, c4-c8). (H,T) = (2,1), g = gl_N or sl_N, kappa = tr. The two-loop obstruction graphs are theta(1,3,3) and theta(2,2,3), with |Aut| = 4, K_{133}(lambda;0) = -(pi/20)[p1 p2][p3 p4] and K_{223}(lambda;0) = +(pi/30)[p1 p2][p3 p4]. Then O_2 = (Nnorm/4) sum_Gamma int dz1 dz2 K_Gamma(d;0) W^Gamma(A,A,A,A) = (pi Nnorm/240) int dz1 dz2 [d1 d2][d3 d4] W_tot, with W_tot = -3 W_133 + 2 W_223. For sl_2: W_tot = -104 k12 k34 + 16 k13 k24 + 40 k14 k23, k_ij = tr(A_i A_j). In the CE complex of g[[z1,z2]] modulo sum p: (i) d omega_133 = d omega_223 = 0. (ii) omega_133 - (3/2) omega_223 = -3(F_133 + F_223) lies in d(C^3) for every N. (iii) [O_2] = (pi Nnorm/48)[F_223]. (iv) [F_223] = 0 for sl_2 and gl_2, and [F_223] != 0 for sl_N and gl_N for every N >= 3. This is certified by exact rank increases at N = 3, 4, 5 and formally in N for N >= 4. (v) If the relative sign of the two graph terms is reversed, the class becomes +-(pi Nnorm/240)[F_223], so (iv) holds for [O_2] in either case. (vi) dim H^4_{(2,2)} = 4 for gl_N with N >= 5 (stable sample ranks). Since every T=1 one-loop graph vanishes identically (rho_1 = 0), O_2 is the first obstruction. For N >= 3 no local ghost-number-0 counterterm at order hbar^2 cancels it. Nnorm = +-hbar^2/(64 pi^5) is derived only.

Proposition 4 (hCS on C^3, even loops; anomaly-structure b1-b4). Every n-loop obstruction graph with cubic vertices has exactly four external vertices, and K_Gamma = kappa_Gamma Delta^n mod sum p, with Delta = det(p1,p2,p3). Only the sgn^{n+1}-isotypic part of the colour 4-tensor contributes. For even n and reductive g = z + s, this part lies in (Lambda^4 s*)^s = H^4(s) = 0, so the n-loop contribution of the classical vertex vanishes. At n=2: K_{theta133} = -Delta^2/432 and K_{theta223} = 0 mod sum p. The one-loop box, K = -Delta/6, gives a closed, non-exact class for sl_2, gl_2, sl_3, gl_3 and sl_4.

Theorem 5 (twisted maximal SYM on R x C^{H|k}, H+1+k = 5; msym-odd). (a) Q_{2m+1} = 0. (b) The Q_2 graphs are the tight theta graphs with O at a trivalent vertex and Gamma\O a tree: theta(1,2,2) for H=1; theta(1,3,3), theta(2,2,3) for H=2; theta(1,4,4), theta(2,3,4), theta(3,3,3) for H=3. Each has two admissible O positions and deg O = 3. (c) H = k = 2 (5d), with hbar = g^2/4. With Qhat_Gamma built from d_z^m K_Gamma/pi, the equation {Qhat_0, k_A Qhat_A + k_B Qhat_B} = 0 has the one-dimensional solution space k ∝ (1,1): rank 1 on so(3) (798 equations) and so(5) (93789 + 18344 equations). This equals sum_Gamma I_Gamma W_Gamma/|Aut Gamma| with the W_Gamma of S2. On letters without derivatives, Q_2 ∝ int d^2theta [<12><45> T_A/20 - <uw><ab> T_B/30] prod_j delta/delta C^{A_j}(theta). (d) H = 3, k = 1 (7d), so(3): k ∝ (-3,6,1) = 6(-1/2, 1, 1/6). (e) H = 1, k = 3 (3d): Qhat_{theta(1,2,2)} with K = -(pi/3) lambda_B lambda_C is Qhat_0-closed by itself (so(3) and so(5)).
missing_for_publication: Derivation of the overall constant and sign of O_2, Nnorm = +-hbar^2/(64 pi^5) (anomaly-structure c2), and of the relative Wick sign between theta(1,3,3) and theta(2,2,3) (c3). Both are derivation only. The class coefficient pi Nnorm/48 depends on them; its nonvanishing does not.

Treatment of closed order-hbar deformations J_1 (ghost number 0, cubic, weight (1,1)). These shift the order-hbar^2 obstruction by (1/2){J_1,J_1}. Needed: the list of such J_1 for sl_N and gl_N (for gl_N it includes the first-order noncommutative term of Costello 1610.04144), and whether [F_223] lies in the span of their {J_1,J_1} modulo exact terms.

Theorem 3 for other simple g (so_N, sp_N, exceptional); only sl_N and gl_N were computed.
Reading of the TeX of 2407.08667 (Sec. 1 expectation, Thm 1.2, Prop. 3.23) and of 1610.04144 Sec. 9. Both were read only through web extraction (refs/references.md status ext).

Written derivations. No REPORT.md exists for any direction because the harness refused them. msym-odd: an end-to-end position-space check of G = s_n (8 pi^{H+1/2})^{-n} K_Gamma; the Koszul sign of W_Gamma for odd propagators; the overall sign and prefactor i/(128 pi^5) of Q_2 relative to Q_0; resolution of the (-1)^n disagreement with S2 eq-B-norm; so(5) runs for 7d; a statement whether Q_2 lifts any Q_0-cohomology class.

Citation of Balduf-Hu 2503.09558 and Brown-Hu-Panzer 2406.12734 for the Pfaffian form of rho_n and the H=0 values. Neither is cited in S1-S3. Check whether the holomorphic-form description announced in BH Sec. 2.4 has appeared.
risks: Theorem 3 is an obstruction class modulo d of order-hbar^2 counterterms only. A closed order-hbar deformation J_1 with {J_1,J_1} cohomologous to [F_223] would make the class removable by changing the theory at order hbar. This is most relevant for gl_N, which has the noncommutative (Moyal) deformation.

Sign conventions are fragile. Four kernel conventions are in use (K[C3], K_htk, S1, S2/S3). a5 of ht-families was refuted for a sign error at odd H, and anomaly-structure b3 has a labelling sign -1 relative to S2 eq-IA. H^4 dimension (c8) upper bounds rest on sample stability. Non-exactness (c6) is rigorous only if the spanning set of invariant cubic cochains (invariant 3-tensors times 9 monomials, Reynolds) is complete.

The MSYM statements assume S2's twist dictionary: the choice Phi(d xbar^{H+1}) = 2 d tau, hbar = g^2/4, and that twisting commutes with quantization (S2 Sec. 8.2).
